assets.name: Catnip Heist (catnip-heist/, standalone Three.js voxel stealth game)
assets.state: PLAYABLE LOCALLY ONLY, not deployed, not committed. What I ran and saw: `npm test` (vitest) passed 120/120 tests in 10 files. `npm run build` (tsc + vite 8.3.1) succeeded: dist/build/index-CZUgRU0C.js is 838.30 kB (233.09 kB gzip), dist/ is 2.7 MB and public/assets is 1.8 MB. The build warns that assets/fonts/catpaw.woff2 did not resolve at build time. Playwright e2e has 12 tests in e2e/heist.spec.ts. Run 1 failed 9 of them with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED because the local preview server dropped, so that was the environment. Run 2 passed 11 of 12. The one real failure is 'retrying a run does not leak scene objects or draw calls' (spec line 348, expect(...).toBe mismatch). Content: 8 levels, heist-01 to heist-08, each with a solver-proven solution file. 7 of the 8 need both cats. 58 cat breed sheets and 5 guard dog sheets. It also has a Cat Yard hub, stars and unlocks, deterministic replays with hashes, touch, gamepad and keyboard controls, and procedural audio plus a chiptune loop. Deployment: no vercel.json, netlify.toml or .vercel. `git status` shows `?? catnip-heist/`, so the folder is untracked and has never been committed. A grep for 'heist' across client/ finds nothing, so the client does not link to it. docs/plans/catnip-heist-3d.md (v2) says to embed it in the client with backend replay-verified saves through POST /user/catbassadors/live. None of that is built. The package is fully standalone, and its README says it imports nothing from client/backend/cms.
assets.strengths: This is the most polished and most testable new build in the repo, and its engineering is easy to show: 120 unit tests, e2e tests, a deterministic sim, solver-proven levels and replay hashes. It is a static site with no backend, so it can go to a public URL within hours. It is new work, which fits hackathon rules that require building during the event window. It reuses the real Token Tails cat art, so the story is a game about rescuing shelter cats. It runs on web and on phone touch screens.
assets.gaps: 1. No public URL. 2. Not in git, so there is no repo or commit to point to. It must be committed and pushed first, and since it sits in the tokentails-app repo that repo would have to be public or the game split into its own repo. 3. One e2e test fails: 'retry leaks scene objects/draw calls'. 4. No gameplay video. 5. No connection to Token Tails accounts, the backend, NFTs, payments or shelters: no score save, no wallet, nothing on-chain. The only shelter link is the story. That makes it weak for web3, payments or impact tracks unless something is wired in. 6. The JS is one 838 kB chunk and there is a font warning. 7. No players or usage data, because it has never been released.
assets.evidence: catnip-heist/package.json (three ^0.183.2, vite ^8.3.1, vitest ^5.0.2); `npm test` gave Test Files 10 passed, Tests 120 passed; `npm run build` gave dist/build/index-CZUgRU0C.js 838.30 kB / gzip 233.09 kB; `playwright test` run 2 gave 11 passed, 1 failed (e2e/heist.spec.ts:348); src/levels/heist-01..08.json plus *.solution.json; catnip-heist/README.md campaign table; docs/plans/catnip-heist-3d.md sections 1-3 (integration planned, not done); git status `?? catnip-heist/`; grep of client/ for 'heist' finds nothing. Hours breakdown (judgment): commit/push or split repo 0.5-1h, static deploy of dist 1-2h, fix the retry-leak e2e 2-4h, 2-3 min gameplay video 2-3h, submission copy 1-2h. That is about 8-12h, so I used 10. Wiring score saves into the backend per the plan would add about 16-30h.

assets.name: ShelterSplit (funding/framework/tracks/a-build/shelter-split, Solidity USDC payout splitter)
assets.state: TESTED CONTRACT ONLY, not deployed, not integrated. I ran `forge test` and got 41 passed, 0 failed, in 3 suites: ShelterSplit.t.sol 32, Tip20Compat.t.sol 8, DeployShelterSplit.t.sol 1. deployments.json contains exactly `[]`, so nothing is deployed on any chain. Grepping client/ and backend/ for sheltersplit or shelter-split finds nothing, so the app does not use it. It has deploy scripts (script/DeployShelterSplit.s.sol, ProofDisburse.s.sol) and a chains.json target list. The track README says a human must broadcast each deploy.
assets.strengths: It is small and clean: basis-point shelter registry, disburse() pays every active shelter in one transaction, reentrancy guard, pause, two-step ownership, safe transfers for USDT-style tokens, fee-on-transfer safe, no dependencies. It can be deployed to many EVM chains with one script, and one tested contract can feed several EVM or stablecoin programs (Arc, Circle, Base, Arbitrum, Avalanche are named in the track README). It fits payments and impact tracks well.
assets.gaps: 1. No deployment anywhere. Mainnet-gated programs such as Arc Microgrants also need real gas and USDC. 2. No frontend or demo page. 3. No link to the real app: the backend's payments go through Stripe and Stellar, not this contract. 4. No shelter wallets are onboarded, so real disbursements can't be shown. 5. No usage, which makes it a 'hackathon prototype' submission with nothing live on-chain. 6. The source may not be committed: git status shows funding/ untracked, and the track README warns that evidence built from uncommitted source fails the check.
assets.evidence: `forge test` gave 'Ran 3 test suites ... 41 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (41 total tests)'; funding/framework/tracks/a-build/deployments.json = []; funding/framework/tracks/a-build/README.md (a human broadcasts, mainnet gate for Arc); grep of client/ and backend/ finds nothing; git status `?? funding/`. Hours breakdown (judgment): commit and testnet deploy with verification on 1-2 chains 2-4h, a minimal disburse demo page 6-10h, video 2h, draft 2h. That is about 12-18h. Real app wiring (backend calls disburse on purchase) would add about 16-24h.

- Commit 81b31abb ('traction update') removed the Stellar on-chain claims: main contract CBHOJ..., 1.2m transactions, 20.7k wallets, 7.4k on-chain DAU, and the stellarchain.io link. It replaced them with the SEI Dune link and cut X followers from 200k to 186k and Instagram from 4.8k to 4.7k.

Not found anywhere in the repo: a count of shelters funded, revenue, donation amounts, or portrait sales. There are also no current or recent figures; all of them are peaks. Catnip Heist and ShelterSplit have zero users or on-chain activity: the heist was never released, and ShelterSplit's deployments.json is [].

So the only verifiable traction is the Token Tails legacy app. None of it counts toward the new Catnip Heist or ShelterSplit builds, and the on-chain numbers are for SEI, not Stellar. Shelter impact and revenue are UNKNOWN.

The general pool outside the Solana track has 23 paid slots (1+20+2), plus unpublished ecosystem-track slots. History: Cypherpunk had 9,000+ participants and 1,576 submissions, with about 33 paid (1 grand, 6 tracks x 5, 2 special), about 2.1%. Frontier had 2,857 submissions and 28 paid (1+25+2), about 1.0%, plus 16 unpaid honorable mentions. If World's Fair keeps the Cypherpunk ratio of about 5.7 builders per submission, it will have about 1,250 or more submissions. 23 general slots against that is about 1.8%. Track 1sts were Capitola (prediction-market aggregator, Consumer), Yumi Finance (BNPL), Seer (tx debugger, infra), Autonom (oracle), MCPay (payments infra) and attn.markets (revenue tokenization). The Consumer top 5 had no game: Capitola, Superfan, Fora, Toaster.trade, Nomu. Cypherpunk had no Gaming track. Breakout (https://blog.colosseum.com/announcing-the-winners-of-the-solana-breakout-hackathon/) did have a Gaming track: Crypto Fantasy League 1st ($25k), Chosendotfun, Scrim, Block Stranding, Lana Roads. The game-like winners were speculative or competitive: WeLikeSports (fantasy), One Arena (TCG battles), The Syndicate (mafia card game), Traded.gg (TCG aggregation). Pattern: most winners are infra, DeFi, payments or prediction markets. The few games that win are wager or fantasy formats, not narrative or casual games.
programs.favors: Consumer traction and venture-scale startups: TAM, revenue, founder-market fit. The rubric does not reward a playable game as such, and it counts traction and revenue. The Catnip Heist 3D voxel stealth game gains nothing on these criteria unless it ships with crypto-native mechanics and real users. The shelter-cat consumer app with real paying users and shelter payouts fits better than ShelterSplit infra or the game. Estimated P(any paid prize) is about 2-4%, below the 10% bar.

S1 (a ShelterSplit USDC payout rail with one real shelter payout) can enter 6 of the 17 programs. It clears the P>10% bar in exactly one of them: Arc Microgrants, where P = 0.12 x 1.5 = 0.18 but the payout is only $500. The other five eligible programs all fall below 10%:
- Colosseum: 0.02 (rubric rewards traction and revenue).
- Arbitrum Dubai: 0.065.
- Team1 Avalanche: 0.05.
- Mezo: 0.05 (shallow MUSD use is penalised, and the prize is paid in tokens).

scored.summary:
Strategy S3 (put Catnip Heist into game-first programs, no crypto) is not the best option, and the numbers show why. The finished heist game has no open cash-prize contest it can enter:
- The contests that would suit it are closed: Vibe Jam, IGF and the Arbitrum DDA gaming grants.
- Every open jam requires new work made during the event: Micro Jam, Terror Jam and Eclipse.
- Creative Europe rules out finished (production-phase) games and puzzle games.

Only three kinds of program accept it:
- **Anitya World Jam.** It does not take the game itself, only a new Anitya world built from the heist's voxel assets. P = 0.15 x 0.9 x 0.75 = 0.101, for a mid prize of about $700 and about 25 human hours.
- **Reddit Developer Funds.** A payout threshold, not a contest. P = 0.4 x 0.1 = 0.04 for $500. All key facts, including whether Lithuania is eligible, are unverified.
- **Farcaster Developer Rewards.** P is about 0.02 for about $75. It has no base rate, no audience for Token Tails, and pays in USDC.

Totals:
- totalEV is about $92 (Anitya $70.9, Reddit $20, Farcaster $1.5, Remix about $0).
- pAtLeastOneWin = 1 - (0.899 x 0.98 x 0.96 x 0.99) = 0.163, assuming the programs are independent.

Only Anitya comes near the P>10% bar, at 10.1%, and it has a 25% risk that no one is judged or paid. Variants that build a new game on the heist engine all fall below the bar: Eclipse 0.024, Terror Jam about 0.06, and Micro Jam/Ziva about 0.10 but worth only about $20.

Compared with the crypto options that S3 skips, the heist is the more polished build but the worse funding asset. Arc Microgrants, with ShelterSplit deployed to Arc mainnet, starts from a higher base rate (0.12), and its judges say promise counts for more than traction. No fit multiplier above 1 was used anywhere without explicit evidence, except Eclipse (x2), where the rules explicitly allow engine boilerplate.

Recommendation: use the heist assets for the Anitya jam (deadline 2026-10-21) as a low-cost side bet, not as the main funding plan.

verdict.proof:
1) The claim that S1 is a 'perfect' plan fails on its own numbers. S1 has exactly one program above the 10% bar: Arc, corrected from 0.18 to 0.15, paying $500 (EV $75). S1's P(at least one win) is 0.30 if the programs are independent. Since all six entries reuse one contract with zero usage, the realistic figure is about 0.20-0.25. About 88% of S1's $1,050 EV comes from programs below 10% (Colosseum, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Circle).

2) The inflation checks. S1's Arc fit of 1.5 relied on 'one real shelter payout', but no shelter wallet exists. S2's scorer rated the same contract alone at a fit of about 1.0-1.1, so I used 1.25 and P 0.15. S1's Arbitrum fit of 1.3 rested on code quality while scoring 0 on users, so I cut it to 1.0 and P 0.05. S2 contains S1's contract, so S2 cannot score lower on the same criteria. I set Arc to 0.155 and Arbitrum to 0.065 there. Colosseum at 1.0-2.8% historical paid rates (about 23 general slots against about 1,250 projected submissions) keeps 0.02; past game winners were wager or fantasy formats. The Mezo 0.10 base is unpublished and its tokens fail the cash rule. Anitya at 0.10 = 0.15 x 0.9 x 0.75 is borderline, not above the bar.

3) Maximising P(at least one win). Crypto programs judge the same asset, so adding more of them gives diminishing, correlated gains. Anitya is judged on a different asset by different judges, so it adds almost its full 0.10 to the combined probability. S1-lean + Anitya reaches 0.340, against 0.267 for S1-lean and 0.317 for S2. S2 + Anitya reaches 0.386, but that +0.046 over H-lean costs 27 more hours, and the S2-over-S1 deltas (+0.005 Arc, +0.015 Arbitrum) are smaller than the estimation error, so it is not strictly better.

4) Maximising EV per human hour. S1-lean gives $1,000 / 39h = $25.6/h, S1 $20.6/h, H-lean $16.7/h, S2 $16.6/h and S3 $1.4/h. The heist-to-contract wiring earns about $3/h marginal, and Mezo about $4/h.

5) How far S1 is from best. S1-lean is the best on EV per hour, by +$8.9/h over the hybrid. On probability of winning, S1 is NOT the best: it trails the hybrid by 0.073 absolute (0.267 vs 0.340 independent, or about 0.20 vs 0.28 correlated), about 27% fewer relative chances. Under the strict P>10% bar, S1 is Arc only (P 0.15), while the hybrid is Arc + Anitya (P 0.235), a gain of +0.085.

6) Catnip Heist on its own (S3) reaches only 0.153 and EV $92. It is the most polished build in the repo, but no open cash program scores that polish. Its value is as the source of Anitya assets and as a diversifier.

All base rates marked 'assumed' (Arc 0.12, Avalanche 0.05, Arbitrum 0.05, Mezo 0.10) are unpublished, so every P here has a range of roughly x0.5 to x1.7. The ranking (hybrid for P, S1-lean for EV per hour, S2 dominated, S3 weakest) holds across that range, because the differences come from the structure of the plans (shared assets and hours) rather than from the point estimates.
